newsitem.title: USA: Telecomms' Primestar offers dishes for sale.
newsitem.headline: Telecomms' Primestar offers dishes for sale.

text.p: Primestar by TCI, a direct broadcast service (DBS) offered by Tele-Communications Inc, announced on Friday new packaging options, including letting the customer buy the satellite dish for the first time.
Up until now, Primestar dishes have been leased by the customers and the company had advertised that as superior to its competitors from whom customers buy their satellite dishes.
Customers for $199 can buy a complete Primestar system when they buy a year of PrimeEntertainment programming.
EchoStar Communications Corp recently lowered its dish price to $199.
Customers who buy the satellite dish will pay $22.99 a month for programming and those who lease will pay $32.99 a month.

Gary Howard, president of TCI Satellite Entertainment Inc, said the moves did not reflect a "price war." He said Primestar's offer was different from its competitors by being the sole operator to offer a premium movie channel, Starz!
The company plans to spend about $8 million in advertising for the remainder of the year, said Kim Gordon, vice president of marketing.

Howard said the new options, which were implemented after consumer surveys were taken, allow customers to "have it both ways." He also said the lower prices for satellite dishes played a role in Primestar's decision to offer dishes for sale.
Howard also announced on a teleconference call that Primestar starting Friday would offer National Hockey League games on its service.
Howard Primestar has 1.4 million customers, giving it about 43-45 percent of the DBS market. It offers its service in a little more than 40 states, covering from 42-44 percent of the United States.
